_description: Every pop-up window, by id. Map '!' markers, HUD buttons and the flow open pop-ups by these ids. Each pop-up: 'title', 'body' (a list of blocks, shown top to bottom), optional 'button' (label of the closing button; default from ui.json). Block types: {"type":"text","text":...} a paragraph; {"type":"stat","value":"5M gal","label":...} a big number; {"type":"citation","text":...,"url":optional} a source line; {"type":"image","illustration":"valley-home","caption":optional} a built-in picture (same names as the intro slides); {"type":"bill","items":[{"label":"Electricity","before":95,"after":160}],"totalLabel":"You now owe","total":optional (default = sum of the increases),"currency":"$","beforeLabel","afterLabel","note"} a bill with increases in red; {"type":"audioPlayer","sound":"datacenter","label":...,"autoplay":true|false} play/pause and volume for a sound in audio.json; {"type":"keys","rows":[{"keys":["W","A"],"label":...}]} keyboard keys with what they do (write "↑", "↓", "←", "→" for arrow keys; they are drawn as arrows).
_usedIn: Simulation page → pop-ups over the game (controls, '!' markers, later HUD buttons)

controls._location: Shown over the valley right after '6 months later'
controls.title: How to play

body.text: Walk Alex around Datadew Valley. Look for the ! markers and read what changed after the data center arrived.

rows.label: Or walk with the arrow keys
Read a ! when you are next to it

body.text: This experience uses sound. Headphones are recommended.

vegetation-loss._location: Valley: '!' on the cleared land beside the data center
vegetation-loss.title: PLACEHOLDER: Where the woods were

body.text: PLACEHOLDER: Acres of forest were cleared to build the data center. The trees that shaded the river and sheltered birds are now stumps.

community._location: Valley: '!' in the town plaza next to the well
community.title: PLACEHOLDER: The town

body.text: PLACEHOLDER: The data center promised jobs, but once it was built it needed only a few dozen workers. Neighbors talk about the noise, the trucks and their bills.

river-contamination._location: Valley: the river (it glows when Alex is near); '!' beside Alex's side of the river
river-contamination.title: PLACEHOLDER: The river

body.text: PLACEHOLDER: Since the data center opened, the river has turned a murky light brown. Wastewater and runoff from the site drain into it, and neighbors no longer let their kids swim here.

bills._location: Valley: Alex's mailbox (the red '-$'), in front of the cottage
bills.title: PLACEHOLDER: This month's bills

body.text: PLACEHOLDER: Data centers use huge amounts of electricity and water, and local utility prices went up to pay for new power lines and water supply.

body.note: PLACEHOLDER: more than before, every month

air-quality-smog._location: Valley: '!' east of the data center, in the smog
air-quality-smog.title: PLACEHOLDER: The air

body.text: PLACEHOLDER: Backup diesel generators and constant power demand put pollution into the air. On still days a haze hangs over the valley.

individual-health._location: HUD: clicking Alex's portrait or name (top-left)
individual-health.title: PLACEHOLDER: How Alex feels

body.text: PLACEHOLDER: Alex sleeps badly with the constant hum, gets headaches and coughs more on smoggy days. Worry about bills and the river weighs on them too.
PLACEHOLDER: Physical and mental health effects of living near a data center.

noise-pollution._location: HUD: clicking the speaker button (bottom-left); the recording starts playing
noise-pollution.title: PLACEHOLDER: The sound of a data center

body.label: Listen: what it sounds like next to a data center

body.text: PLACEHOLDER: Cooling fans and transformers run day and night. Neighbors describe a low hum and a high whine they can hear even indoors.
